newsitem.title: USA: Antex starts ear infection vaccine Phase I.
newsitem.headline: Antex starts ear infection vaccine Phase I.

text.p: Antex Biologics Inc said on Wednesday it and Pasteur Merieux Connaught, a wholly owned subsidiary of Rhone-Poulenc began Phase I clinical trial for a Haemophilus influenza vaccine.
Haemophilus influenza causes otitis media or the common inner ear infection, the company said.

The vaccine was being developed by Pasteur Merieux Connaught through a technology license agreement with Antex, it said, adding that there were no vaccines on the market to prevent or treat the common ear infection.
The vaccine consists of a recombinant form of a patented H. influenza outer membrane protein, called Hin47, in combination with an adjuvant, the company said.
Hin47 was identified by Antex scientists using one of the company's core technologies, Adhesin-Receptor technology.
The Phase I clinical trial was an open monocenter study to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of the Hin47 protein as an otitis media vaccine in healthy adults, Antex said.
Haemophilus influenza causes over 25 million cases of inner ear infections in children and infants annually in the United States alone, Antex said.
